title: The young men in the cave
hook: young believers flee to a cave and pray, our Lord, grant us mercy and set right our affair (18:10)

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Friday surah, al-Kahf, and your line was friday's surah. Is it in your calendar yet, with a time and a place? Day four hundred sixty-four.

A handful of young men in a city where their faith has become dangerous. Their people, the surah says, have taken other gods beside the One. They can stay and pretend, or they can go. They go. Out past the edge of town, up into the hills, into a cave in the rock, with nothing but each other and a dog. And the first thing they do, once they're inside and the noise is gone, is ask for something. Today: what they ask.

The Qur'an calls them fitya, young men, youths. Verse thirteen says they believed in their Lord, and God increased them in guidance. Verse fourteen says God bound their hearts firm when they stood up and said: our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth. Then they withdrew. And at the cave mouth, in Pickthall's translation of verse ten: "Our Lord! Give us mercy from Thy presence, and shape for us right conduct in our plight." Look at the two halves. Mercy from Your presence: min ladunk, from with You, straight from God rather than from the people around them. And then: arrange for us, out of our affair, rashad, right guidance, a sound way through. They don't ask to win. They don't ask for their enemies to fall. They ask for mercy and for their situation to be set straight. What happens next is that God puts them to sleep, which we'll come to tomorrow. The Qur'an doesn't name the city or the century. It mentions ar-Raqim, a word commentators explain in different ways: an inscribed tablet, a place, a valley. Christians tell a story of sleepers in a cave near Ephesus, and some Muslim commentators connected the two; the Qur'an itself leaves the details open, and warns, a few verses on, against arguing about them. What it keeps is the prayer. Muslims still say it, word for word in Arabic, when a situation is beyond them: rabbana atina min ladunka rahmah, wa hayyi' lana min amrina rashada. It's the prayer of people who've done the one thing they could do, which was to leave, and hand the rest over.
screen: `FITYA: YOUNG MEN, HEARTS MADE FIRM.` · `MERCY FROM YOUR PRESENCE.` · `SET OUR AFFAIR STRAIGHT.` · `NO CITY, NO CENTURY, NAMED.` · then, large: `SHAPE FOR US RIGHT CONDUCT IN OUR PLIGHT.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one situation in your life that's tangled: a job, a family knot, a decision with no clean answer. Picture yourself stepping out of it for two minutes, the way they stepped into the cave. Let the noise drop. If you pray, you can say their du'a, in Arabic or in your own language: our Lord, give us mercy from Your presence, and set right our affair. If you don't, just hold the situation without trying to fix it, and let it be held. The bell holds the time.
Fitya. The young men who left a city turned from God, and asked for mercy and a straight way through. Today's word.
Your line: set right our affair. Today, when something gets tangled, do the one thing in your power, then let go of the rest. Day four hundred sixty-four.

howItsDone: The du'a of 18:10 is memorized by Muslims and said in Arabic when facing a difficult situation; it's also recited as part of al-Kahf on Fridays.

fork.setup: you and your friends have fled a city where your faith is dangerous. you reach the cave. what do you ask for?
options: for the city to be punished.
mercy from God's presence, and your affair set right.
to be made rulers of the city.
fork.reveal: mercy, and right conduct in their plight (18:10). they ask for guidance through, not for victory.

original.script: رَبَّنَا آتِنَا مِن لَّدُنكَ رَحْمَةً وَهَيِّئْ لَنَا مِنْ أَمْرِنَا رَشَدًا
original.say: RAB-ba-naa AA-ti-naa min la-DUN-ka RAH-ma-tan wa HAY-yi' la-naa min AM-ri-naa ra-SHA-daa
original.note: Arabic: the young men's prayer (18:10): our Lord, give us mercy from Your presence, and arrange right guidance for us in our affair.

trapdoor: what you thought: some young men hid in a cave.
what it means: youths who refused to pretend left their city and asked only for mercy and a straight way through.
what a scholar hears: min ladunk marks mercy coming directly from God's presence; ar-Raqim's meaning is debated in tafsir.

sources.quoted: Our Lord! Give us mercy from Thy presence, and shape for us right conduct in our plight.

notes: Pickthall wording of 18:10 quoted from memory; confirm exactly.
Arabic of the du'a (18:10) and its transliteration: confirm.
Mention of the Christian Seven Sleepers of Ephesus is brief and neutral; confirm a Keeper is comfortable with it.
Ar-Raqim meanings (tablet, place, valley) summarized from tafsir; confirm.
Editor review (2026-10-01): hook now follows 18:15 ('their people'), not families and rulers; trimmed the interpretive gloss on min ladunk; 'many commentators/Muslims' claims softened.
